entries.effect: the path as the assistive technology sees it: converted through the view's own window and then through that window's screen space, with the transform between views read off three converted points so a rotated or flipped view is converted as it really is, and the path itself when the view is in no window
entries.source: the same chain as UIAccessibilityConvertFrameToScreenCoordinates, which the tree already carries in UIKit+Constants7c.m; the header of SDK 26.2 for the two-argument shape

entries.effect: NO: the release carries no AssistiveTouch state to read, measured on its own cache where the only AssistiveTouch names are AssistiveTouchCustomGestureCreation and AssistiveTouchPID, neither of which is a state, and it exposes no notification the state changes through. This is the answer a device with AssistiveTouch off gives, and it is the seam the whole push allows rather than a guess
entries.source: the release's own 6.1.3 dyld shared cache, for what it carries; the host's own UIKit under Mac Catalyst for the answer a system with the feature off gives

entries.effect: UIAccessibilityHearingDeviceEarNone: this device has no paired hearing device, so there is no ear, which is the answer the release documents for no device
entries.source: the host's own UIKit under Mac Catalyst, where no hearing device is paired either

entries.effect: the handler is called with NO: a guided access session is a state the system puts the whole device into and only the system's own guided access starts one, so an application asking is answered as an application that did not get one, and a caller waiting on the handler is not left waiting
entries.source: the host's own UIKit under Mac Catalyst, which answers the same way when no guided access session is running

entries.effect: UIGuidedAccessRestrictionStateAllow for every identifier: the release keeps its restrictions where an application cannot read them and exposes no query for one, and Allow is the header's own initial state for every restriction and what a device outside guided access answers
entries.source: the header of SDK 26.2 for the initial state; the host's own UIKit for the answer outside guided access
